title: structured-output: constrained-decoding backends - CFG/regex backends + tokenizer edgecase fixes
author: Evan Park
description:
Motivation: Structured output constraints (CFG/grammar, regex-based constraints) are critical for stable tool/function calling and deterministic structured responses. We have observed multiple customer reports and internal test failures where constraints accepted at the token-sequence API level were violated in practice due to tokenizer edgecases (subword boundaries, leading/trailing whitespace, and non-UTF8 tokens) and mismatch between regex engines applied on text vs token streams. This PR introduces two constrained-decoding backends (token-aware regex automaton and a CFG-to-FST path), fixes tokenizer handling in the constrained-decoding pipeline, and wires the OpenAI-compat layer to surface structured constraint inputs through the policy router.

Design summary: 1) Add a token-aware regex backend that compiles user regex into a DFA over token IDs instead of raw characters; this avoids mismatches when regexes are intended to apply to decoded text but constraints must be enforced during token-by-token generation. 2) Implement a CFG -> FST lowering path for simple grammars (subset useful for tool responses) so we can enforce hierarchical constraints efficiently at decode time. 3) Harden tokenizer handling: canonicalize input by preserving leading/trailing whitespace tokens, handle byte-level fallback tokens, and add a normalization step to align decoder tokens with the regex/CFG engines. 4) Add tests covering previously failing edgecases (non-breaking spaces, surrogate pairs, and multi-token punctuation) and add an integration test that runs the OpenAI-compatible /v1/responses flow with structured constraints.

Implementation details: - New files: redwood/runtime/decoding/constraints_tokenregex.py (token-DFA compilation and matcher), redwood/runtime/decoding/cfg_to_fst.py (CFG lowering), and a small helper redwood/runtime/decoding/token_normalizer.py. - Existing decoder pipeline (redwood/runtime/decoding/decoder.py) updated to accept a 'constraint_backend' argument with choice ["text_regex", "token_regex", "cfg_fst"]. Backwards compatible default remains text_regex. - OpenAI compatibility: redwood/sdk-python/redwood/openai_compat.py updated to accept the new structured constraints payload (keeps previous fields but forwards the raw constraint blob in metadata); server-side routing in redwood/api/handlers/responses_handler.py now validates and attaches a constraint_backend hint based on constraint size/complexity. - Tests: redwood/tests/unit/test_constraints.py, redwood/tests/integration/test_openai_compat_structured_constraints.py. - Benchmarks: small microbenchmark harness added under perf-canary/constraints_bench to measure runtime overhead.

Testing and CI: Initial CI failed on a flaky test that surfaced a race between cache eviction and constraint state; I added a deterministic cache eviction hook for tests and re-ran. All unit and integration tests pass. Microbenchmarks show ~12% overhead for conservative token_regex enforcement on p3.2xlarge, and ~25% for complex CFG lowered to FST; we add a runtime knob to prefer text_regex for extremely latency-sensitive routes.

Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind runtime flag 'decoder.constraint_backends' (defaults to text_regex). - Canary release on dedicated fleet for two days, observing P50/P95 latency and constraint violation metrics. - Post-canonicalization we will enable token_regex for internal customers and opt-in for hosted customers via API flag.

Related: fixes regression from PR #38921 (structured-output constrained-decoding tokenization edgecases) and implements acceptance criteria from ENG-2148. Also updates docs and examples in redwood-docs (follow-up PR scheduled).
commits: Initial token-regex backend implementation and unit tests
Add CFG->FST lowering and integration tests
Fix tokenizer normalization edgecases and CI cache hook
OpenAI compat: forward structured constraints and route hints
changed_file_snippets: decoder.py: add parameter constraint_backend and dispatch to backend.match_next(token_id)
constraints_tokenregex.py: compile regex -> token DFA using tokenizer.vocab and return match states
cfg_to_fst.py: lower small CFG (S -> TOOL_RESP) to an FST optimized for prefix checks
openai_compat.py: accept 'structured_constraints' in request body and attach to internal request.metadata['constraints']
review_conversation: Priya Patel: Can you clarify the backward compatibility story for user-provided regexes? We need to ensure existing hosted customers see no behavior change when they don't opt-in.

Evan Park: We keep text_regex as the default and only use token_regex when the customer requests 'backend=token_regex' or when the routing policy upgrades the route after canary. Added note in description.
Liam O'Sullivan: Perf looks acceptable but we should add a CPU/latency guardrail to prevent token_regex from being enabled on low-tier nodes.
Evan Park: Added runtime knob and docs in the benchmark harness; handler now rejects token_regex for nodes with <8GB GPU memory.
Maya Singh: Tests look good. One nits: prefer explicit error message when CFG parse fails rather than generic 500.
Evan Park: Changed CFG parser to raise ConstraintParseError and mapped to 400 with a clear message.
Priya Patel: Approving after the compatibility note is added to SDK docs.
release_notes: Add token-aware regex and CFG->FST constrained decoding backends; fixes several tokenizer edgecases that could violate structured constraints. Default behavior unchanged. Opt-in runtime flag 'decoder.constraint_backends' available. See changelog for details.
notes: This PR fixes multiple customer-reported incidents where function-calling constraints were violated due to tokenizer/regression mismatches. Follow-up: docs PR to include examples of token_regex for common regex patterns and SDK examples for enabling backends via OpenAI-compatible requests.
